Stress test¶

The four-channel loss-of-flow case was run 94 times around its operating point, one parameter at a time. Each case is a fresh build, a toolkit guess, a steady solve, a scram and a 2500 s transient, all in its own process.

Completed means the case reached 2500 s. Saturation means the bulk coolant reached saturation and STREAM stopped with a SaturationReachedError naming the channel and cell: the single-phase model's stated validity boundary. Failed means the solver gave up; timeout, that the case overran its time limit.

The cells read the stored tables in results/; with RECOMPUTE = True each axis re-runs through sweeps.run_axis first.

In [1]:
%matplotlib inline
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parent))
from showcase import plots, sweeps
from showcase.lofa_case import HEATED, TSAT

RECOMPUTE = False
COLUMNS = ["label", "status", "t_open", "t_rev_hot", "t_rev_warm", "t_rev_wide", "peak_hot", "margin",
           "n_warnings", "wall_s"]
FORMATS = dict(t_open="{:.1f}", t_rev_hot="{:.0f}", t_rev_warm="{:.0f}", t_rev_wide="{:.0f}", peak_hot="{:.1f}",
               margin="{:.1f}", wall_s="{:.0f}", residual_entry="{:.3g}")
frames = {}


def load(axis):
    if axis not in frames:
        frames[axis] = sweeps.run_axis(axis) if RECOMPUTE else sweeps.load(axis)
    return frames[axis]


def table(df, columns=COLUMNS):
    formats = {k: v for k, v in FORMATS.items() if k in columns}
    return df[columns].style.format(formats, na_rep="").hide(axis="index")
In [2]:
MARK = dict(
    completed=lambda c: dict(marker="o", color=c),
    saturation=lambda c: dict(marker="o", color=c, markerfacecolor="white",
                              markeredgecolor=plots.STATUS_COLORS["saturation"], markeredgewidth=2),
    failed=lambda c: dict(marker="X", color=plots.STATUS_COLORS["failed"]),
    timeout=lambda c: dict(marker="s", color=plots.STATUS_COLORS["timeout"]),
)


def series(ax, xs, ys, status, color, label=None):
    ax.plot(xs, ys, color=color, label=label)
    for s, kw in MARK.items():
        m = (status == s).to_numpy()
        ax.plot(xs[m], ys[m], linestyle="none", **kw(color))


def saturation(ax, xs, df):
    tsat = np.array([TSAT(p) for p in df["p_p_ref"]])
    if np.ptp(tsat) == 0:
        plots.hline(ax, tsat[0], f"Saturation {tsat[0]:.1f} °C")
        return
    ax.plot(xs, tsat, "--", color=plots.NEUTRAL, linewidth=1.5)
    ax.annotate("Saturation", xy=(xs[-1], tsat[-1]), xytext=(-4, -14), textcoords="offset points", ha="right",
                color=plots.NEUTRAL)
In [3]:
def figure(df, x, xlabel, logx=False, scale=1.0):
    categorical = x == "label"
    df = df if categorical else df.sort_values(x)
    xs = np.arange(len(df)) if categorical else df[x].to_numpy(float) * scale
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3.8), layout="constrained")
    for k in HEATED:
        series(axes[0], xs, df[f"t_rev_{k}"].to_numpy(), df["status"], plots.COLORS[k])
        series(axes[1], xs, df[f"peak_{k}"].to_numpy(), df["status"], plots.COLORS[k])
    series(axes[2], xs, df["t_open"].to_numpy(), df["status"], plots.INK)
    saturation(axes[1], xs, df)
    for ax, ylabel in zip(axes, ("Flow reversal [s]", "Peak coolant temperature [°C]", "Flapper opening [s]")):
        ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
        if logx:
            ax.set_xscale("log")
        if categorical:
            ax.set_xticks(xs, df["label"], rotation=30, ha="right")
    finish(fig, axes, df)
    return fig
In [4]:
def finish(fig, axes, df):
    opening = df["t_open"].dropna()
    if np.ptp(opening) < 8:
        mid = 0.5 * (opening.max() + opening.min())
        axes[2].set_ylim(mid - 4, mid + 4)
    present = [s for s in MARK if (df["status"] == s).any()]
    handles = [Line2D([], [], color=plots.COLORS[k]) for k in HEATED]
    handles += [Line2D([], [], linestyle="none", **MARK[s](plots.NEUTRAL)) for s in present]
    labels = [k.capitalize() for k in HEATED] + [s.capitalize() for s in present]
    fig.legend(handles, labels, loc="outside upper center", ncol=len(labels))


def show(axis, x, xlabel, logx=False, scale=1.0, rows=None):
    df = load(axis)
    df = df[rows(df)] if rows is not None else df
    with plots.style():
        figure(df, x, xlabel, logx, scale)
        plt.show()
    return table(df)

Power¶

Power runs from 0.30 to 1.00 of full; 0.70 is the operating point. The margin falls from 32.2 °C to 5.1 °C at 0.90 and crosses zero before 0.95, where both top rungs stop on saturation in the hot channel. More power brings every reversal earlier.

Saturated points sit about 0.2 °C above the line: the stop uses the pressure in the cell, a little above the reference pressure the line is drawn at.

Pump head¶

A stronger pump opens the flapper sooner (98 s at half head, 62 s at double) and delays the reversals. The peak barely moves. The flapper set point is 30 % of a nominal flow estimated from the pump head and the channel gaps, so along this axis the set point rises with the head.

Flywheel inertia¶

A short coastdown reverses the channels while decay heat is still high: at 0.3 and 0.5 times the default inertia the hot channel saturates, at about 805 s and 1346 s (stops table). At 2 and 3 times some or all reversals fall past the 2500 s window. Those runs complete; the missing points are reversals that had not happened yet.

Channel gaps¶

One gap changes per case. A 1.5 mm hot gap has a quarter less flow area at the same power and saturates at the reversal spike, about 658 s (stops table), before the other channels have warmed. A 3 mm bypass, against 4 mm, weakens natural circulation, and the hot channel creeps to saturation at about 2367 s (stops table). The flapper set point is 30 % of a nominal flow estimated from the pump head and the gaps, so it moves with the gaps too; the opening runs from about 43 s to 167 s across these cases.

System pressure¶

Pressure moves the saturation line and little else: same opening time, reversals within 4 s. The margin goes from 4.9 °C at 1.5 bar to 32.9 °C at 4 bar.

Flapper threshold¶

The flapper opens when the loop flow drops to this fraction of its nominal value. At 0.1 it opens at about 235 s, the natural-circulation path arrives late and the hot channel creeps to saturation.

Flapper area¶

The area does not change the opening time, only what follows. At 0.3 times the default the natural-circulation path is too restrictive and the hot channel saturates at about 1420 s (stops table).

Friction law¶

Blasius under-predicts friction in the laminar natural-circulation regime, so the hot peak comes out lower, about 90 °C against 108 °C. The regime-dependent law, the default, is the physical one.

Solver tolerance¶

The absolute tolerance is atol_rel times each variable's own scale. At atol_rel = 0.1, 30 °C on a temperature, the run stops at 286 s with the hot peak at 66 °C, far from saturation; the error, printed below the figure, names the step failure. At 1e-2 the run completes but the hot reversal moves to about 1094 s against 814 s; at 1e-3 it is off by 8 s. From 1e-4 down the opening, reversals and peak agree within about 0.1 s, 2 s and 0.1 °C.

Trip time (pump trip and scram together)¶

This axis moves the pump trip and the scram together, from 1 to 30 s. The opening goes from about 76 s to 105 s and the reversals move by 26 to 28 s, so the opening stays about 75 s after the trip: the trip time shifts the start of the accident, nothing else. The width of the rod-insertion ramp, 0.1 to 5 s, moves the opening by under 3 s and the peaks by under 1 °C.

Initial guesses¶

The toolkit guess, the closed-form seed, a uniform ballpark, a hand-made expert guess and twenty random ±30 % perturbations of the toolkit guess, with entry residuals from 10.8 to 1.4e6. All 24 complete. Over the 24 rows the steady flows agree to about 1e-7 kg/s, the reversals within one 2 s output step and the warm and wide peaks within about 0.2 °C, the hot peak within 0.003 °C.

The expert guess records three warnings, one per heated channel, printed below. They are raised while the expert guess solves each heated plate alone with symmetric_plate_steady_state, a helper system with a fixed inlet temperature, not by the transient system. The toolkit guess on the same system records none, and the expert run completes.

94 cases ran and 85 completed. The 8 saturation stops sit at the edges of the envelope: power from 0.95, a short coastdown, a narrow hot channel or bypass, a late or small flapper. Each is the hot channel saturating for a physical reason, with the channel and cell named in its error (stops table).

The one failure is the loosest tolerance, which stops at 286 s with the hot peak at 66 °C, far from saturation, and an error naming the step failure. No failure is unexplained, and the default path runs without a warning.
